# Creatures options

<!-- GENERATED by tests/ArcaneCore.World.Tests/Docs (ConfigReferenceRenderer.RenderByArea) from the options classes. Do not edit by hand.
     Regenerate: ARCANECORE_UPDATE_DOCS=1 dotnet test tests/ArcaneCore.World.Tests --filter Docs -->

69 options. Set them in the daemon's `.conf` file or `appsettings.json`. Full reference: [configuration.md](../configuration.md). All areas: [index](README.md).

Daemon says which server reads it. Reload says whether `.reload config` applies it: `live` is applied to the running server, `restart` keeps its value until the next start, `start` is read once when the daemon starts.

## `Creatures`

| `ImplicitEventAi` | `bool` | `false` | true \| false | World | start | `Creatures:ImplicitEventAi` (default off, retail): vmangos runs EventAI only for a template whose `AIName` is 'EventAI' (AI/CreatureAISelector.cpp:37-100, AI/EventAI/CreatureEventAI.cpp:51-56), and classic-db z2815 carries that column (`creature_template.AIName`, 4,325 templates say 'EventAI'; imported by CreatureDumpImporter). Switched on, a creature whose template has no AIName but whose entry (or spawn) has `creature_ai_scripts` rows also runs EventAI, the cmangos-classic permit (AI/EventAI/CreatureEventAI.cpp:51-63) for hand-edited data; an explicit AIName always wins. A deviation from retail. |

Retail (false): vmangos CreatureAI::EnterEvadeMode sets neither (AI/CreatureAI.cpp:323-346); health and mana return through the creature's own regeneration, a third of the maximum every 5 s (Objects/Creature.cpp:1087-1160). |
| `Movement:HonorWaypointRunColumn` | `bool` | `false` | true \| false | World | start | `Creatures:Movement:HonorWaypointRunColumn`: a waypoint node whose `creature_movement.Run` column is set is travelled at run speed. Not retail: the column exists in neither classic-db nor vmangos (an ArcaneCore addition of the creature-AI step); vmangos waypoint legs walk unless the creature runs by default (`SetWalk(!UNIT_STATE_RUNNING ...)`, Movement/WaypointMovementGenerator.cpp:240). |
| `Movement:MissingWaypointPathFallback` | `MissingWaypointPathFallback` | `Random` | Random \| Idle | World | start | `Creatures:Movement:MissingWaypointPathFallback`: what a creature with waypoint movement but no path (neither its spawn's `creature_movement` rows nor its entry's `creature_movement_template` path) does. Both references leave it standing (vmangos WaypointMovementGenerator::LoadPath, Movement/WaypointMovementGenerator.cpp:47-52, logs and keeps an empty path); that is `MissingWaypointPathFallback.Idle`. The default, `MissingWaypointPathFallback.Random`, is a deliberate deviation: the creature wanders within its spawn's wander distance (5 yd when the spawn has none) so a content gap does not leave a patrol frozen in place. The content audit reports such spawns once at load either way. Values: `Random`, `Idle`. |
| `Movement:MonsterMoveOffsetBase` | `MonsterMoveOffsetBase` | `Destination` | Destination \| Midpoint | World | start | `Creatures:Movement:MonsterMoveOffsetBase`. `MonsterMoveOffsetBase.Destination` is retail; the midpoint layout is the pre-fidelity ArcaneCore behaviour, kept only as a rollback switch. Values: `Destination`, `Midpoint`. |
| `Movement:PathJobThreads` | `int` | `4` | a whole number, -2147483648 to 2147483647 | World | start | `Creatures:Movement:PathJobThreads`: the path-job threads (`PathJobs`), shared by every map; 1-64. They run below normal priority. Read once, when the first map starts the pool. |
| `Movement:PathJobs` | `bool` | `false` | true \| false | World | start | `Creatures:Movement:PathJobs`: run the navmesh searches of out-of-combat creature moves (wander, waypoint, point and scripted moves, evade/home returns of walkers) and of chases (in or out of combat, a pet's included) on a pool of path-job threads instead of the map's update (multithreading plan W5). The answer is the same search over the same loaded tiles; the creature starts the move on a later update, as it does today when the per-update search budget is spent (a chaser already running takes its answer mid-spline only with `PathJobsFollow` on too). A search a worker has been running for 5 s (`CreatureMapSystem.PathJobPendingTimeoutMs`) is dropped and asked again; time a job waits in the pool's queue does not count, so a busy pool keeps its queue in order. Follow and formation searches join the pool only with `PathJobsFollow`; flee, confused and flier searches and a pet's other moves stay synchronous. Off by default; read when the map's creature system starts. |
| `Movement:PathJobsFollow` | `bool` | `false` | true \| false | World | start | `Creatures:Movement:PathJobsFollow`: out-of-combat follow searches (pets and escorts following their leader) go to the path-job pool too (`PathJobs` must be on). The follower keeps its current spline until the answer arrives (one or two updates); an answer whose destination is within `CreatureMapSystem.PathJobFollowTolerance` (1 yd) of the re-asked one still applies, since a leader on the move shifts the follow point every update. A slower answer is still waited for, and walked when the path it found ends closer to the leader's new point than the follower stands; a lagging answer with no path, or one ending farther away, is asked again. A follower, formation member or chaser already on a spline takes its answer mid-spline: while it has only run on along that spline (up to `CreatureMapSystem.PathJobCarryYards`, 4 yd) its job is waited for, not dropped and asked again, and the path is re-anchored at where it now stands, dropping corners it has already passed, so behind a running leader it keeps running with one job in flight. On a map with navigation the new first leg is walked on the navmesh with the path's own options; it is refused (asked again from where the creature stands) when the creature cannot be placed on the mesh, the walk is blocked, or it ends on another layer. A map without navigation takes the leg unchecked. Chase searches use the pool whenever `PathJobs` is on; only with this setting does a running chaser take answers mid-spline too, otherwise its answer is dropped and asked again once it has run past the answer's start. |
| `Movement:PathJobsWander` | `bool` | `false` | true \| false | World | start | `Creatures:Movement:PathJobsWander`: with `PathJobs` on, a wander leg's random-point pick and its path search run as one job on the path-job pool, and the creature idles until the answer is applied on the map's thread. The map's RNG gives one draw per leg (the seed); the point of a leg is a pure function of (seed, centre, radius, loaded navmesh). The same map seed and tile state give the same legs when each job is applied on the same update (as a test that waits for the pool each tick does); in a live server worker timing can move a leg's apply update and with it the later draws from the map RNG. The leg starts one update later than the synchronous route. Needs `PathJobs`; off by default (opt-in, like `PathJobsFollow`). Off keeps the synchronous point pick and today's RNG draws exactly. |
| `Movement:RunDuringWanderChancePercent` | `uint` | `15` | a whole number, 0 to 4294967295 | World | start | `Creatures:Movement:RunDuringWanderChancePercent`: for a creature with the cmangos RUN_DURING_WANDER flag, the percent of random-movement legs that run (cmangos MotionGenerators/RandomMovementGenerator.cpp:135-136: `SetWalk(urand(0, 99) &gt;= 15)`). vmangos has no such flag (its 0x20 is NO_MOVEMENT_PAUSE), so the setting only reaches creatures imported in the cmangos dialect. |
| `MovementEnabled` | `bool` | `true` | true \| false | World | start | Random and waypoint movement; off leaves every creature idle at its spawn point. |
| `NoMeleeFleeMs` | `uint` | `30000` | a whole number, 0 to 4294967295 | World | start | How long a NO_MELEE_FLEE creature runs before it evades (cmangos `DoFlee(30000)`, Unit.cpp:7996). |
| `NoMeleeFleeOnAggro` | `bool` | `false` | true \| false | World | start | `Creatures:NoMeleeFleeOnAggro` (default false): a creature with the static flag NO_MELEE_FLEE (0x00100000) that a player or a player's pet engages runs in panic for `NoMeleeFleeMs` and then evades (cmangos Unit::SetInCombatWithVictim, Entities/Unit.cpp:7993-7998, and CreatureAI::TimedFleeingEnded, AI/BaseAI/CreatureAI.cpp:254-258). vmangos only takes the melee away for the same bit (CREATURE_STATIC_FLAG_NO_MELEE, whose original comment is "Flee"; AI/CreatureAI.cpp:40), and the default keeps that, since vmangos is the fidelity reference; critters still run from a hit through CritterAI either way. Melee is off for the flag either way. classic-db z2815 sets it on 71 templates (deer, sheep, cows, wisps, totems, target dummies). |

The count (vmangos m_targetNotReachableTimer, :1013-1030) runs while the chase on top of the creature's movement says its victim is unreachable, the creature is not a ranged chaser, not owned or charmed by a player, has no NO_UNREACHABLE_EVADE flag and cannot hit the victim (out of melee reach or out of sight); it restarts at 0 whenever that stops being true and when combat ends. 0 disables the evade; EventAI's EVENT_T_TARGET_NOT_REACHABLE still fires. |

Attacks on it evade (it counts for `Creature.IsInEvadeMode`), its AI does not update (Creature.cpp:1041) and it regenerates as if out of combat (:1057); it keeps its victim and keeps chasing. 0 disables this stage. |
